transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well... I suppose it's mostly my sleep. I just barely sleep in any useful way anymore. 

I'll just lie awake replaying client models in my head. And then I usually wake up at 3 or 4 in the morning anyway, with my stomach all tight. Then I just have to go to work feeling like I never actually rested. So... that's why I'm here.
How long have you been having trouble sleeping like this?
It's been... a while. About three years, I suppose. Ever since the merger reorganized our Caribbean-market division.
Do you often feel anxious or worried about things in general, even when there isn't a clear reason for it?
I don't think so. I mean... there's usually a reason. It's just work. I don't really sit around worrying about nothing, if that's what you're asking.
Do you ever find yourself feeling very anxious or on edge about a number of different things, even when those worries seem bigger than the actual problem?
No... not really. Like I said, it's just work. I don't... I don't just worry about everything. It's just the models and the division. That's all.
Have you been feeling down or losing interest in things you usually enjoy, even outside of work?

I guess... yeah. It's just... most days, I have this heavy, gray feeling. Even at my apartment, not just the office. I'm just going through the motions. And... sometimes someone will just ask me a normal question, and I... I have to try really hard not to cry. That's... yeah.
Have you noticed that you don't enjoy things as much as you used to, or that you've lost interest in activities you once found pleasurable?
I don't really know. I don't do much anymore, so... it's hard to say. I just go home and try to rest. I haven't really tried to do anything fun in a long time.
Have you been feeling down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, not just occasionally or in response to specific stressors?
I don't really know. I... I don't keep track of it like that. It's just... like I said before, it's just that heavy feeling. I'm not sure if it's every single day.
Would you say that the heavy, gray feeling you described is present most of the day, nearly every day, even when there isn't anything specific happening at work?

I mean... yes, I suppose. It's... it's most days. That heavy feeling... it's just there, whether I'm at the office or at my apartment. I just... go through the motions. And like I said, it doesn't take much to make me feel like I might cry. Even just a normal question. It's... just there.
Would you say that the heavy, gray feeling you mentioned has been present most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks at a time?
I... I suppose. I don't really track it in weeks. It just... it all kind of blends together. I'm not sure.
Have you noticed that you don’t take pleasure in things you used to enjoy, even small things like a good meal, a TV show, or time with friends?

I don't know. I guess I just... I don't really do much anyway. Work takes up most of my time. I just come home and... I don't know, I just exist, I suppose. I haven't really thought about whether I enjoy things or not.
Have you lost interest in things you used to enjoy, even small things like a good meal, a TV show, or time with friends?
I... you just asked me that. About not enjoying things. I don't... I don't really have a different answer. I just go to work, come home... that's it. I don't really have hobbies anymore.
Would you say that your mood feels low even on days when nothing particularly stressful or upsetting has happened at work?

I guess so. It doesn't really matter if it's stressful or not. Most days I just... move through the office, or even my apartment, with that same heavy, gray feeling. I'm just going through the motions. Sometimes someone will ask me a completely normal question and I... I just have to try really hard not to cry. So... yeah. Even on quiet days.
Have you felt a noticeable loss of energy or felt fatigued nearly every day, even when you haven't been doing much physically or mentally?
I don't... I don't really know. I mean, I'm tired, but... I work a lot. So, it's hard to tell if it's just normal tiredness or... something else. I just sleep when I can.
Have you been feeling worthless or guilty, even about small things, nearly every day?

I suppose so. It's... well, at work, if a manager questions one of my financial projections, even just a routine check, I... I just assume it's because I'm slipping. I immediately think they know I'm not as sharp as I used to be, and that everyone can see I'm failing. It just feels like I'm not good enough anymore.
Have you had days in a row where you felt that heavy, gray feeling and didn't enjoy things, even for small moments, for at least two weeks straight?

I'm... not really sure. I don't keep track of the days like that. It all just sort of blends together, so... I don't think it's been two weeks straight without any small moments at all. But I don't really know.
Would you say that the heavy, gray feeling you've described has been present most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks in a row at any point?

I suppose... yes. Most days it's like that. I just... I move through the office, or even when I'm back at my apartment, and it's just this... heavy, gray feeling. Like I'm just going through the motions. Most of the day, I'm just... trying not to cry when someone asks me a normal question. So, yes... I guess it's been there for at least that long.
Have you found that you’ve completely lost interest in things you used to enjoy, even things you used to look forward to, like hobbies, food, or spending time with people?

I don't... I wouldn't say completely. I mean, I still eat when I need to. And I don't really have a lot of hobbies anyway, mostly just work. So... no, I don't think I've completely lost interest in everything. I just... I haven't really noticed that.
Have you noticed that it's been harder to focus, make decisions, or think clearly because of how you've been feeling?

I suppose... yes. It's been harder. At work, I mean. Spreadsheets that used to be... well, second nature... they take me hours now. I just... I lose the thread of what I'm doing. I end up rereading the same assumptions over and over. And even then, I still worry I've missed something obvious before a presentation. So, yes... it's harder to think clearly.
